EXL3 kernels based on ExLlamaV3, adapted via Project Maya for Fastllm

Primary algorithm reference: ExLlamaV3 by Turboderp
https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3
Copyright (c) 2025 Turboderp; MIT license: LICENSE.exllamav3.

ExLlamaV3 is the source of the EXL3 format, codebooks, trellis-window arithmetic
and tensor-core tile decoding used by these adapted kernels. Its relevant
sources are exllamav3/exllamav3_ext/quant/codebook.cuh, exl3_dq.cuh and
hadamard_inner.cuh. The imported Maya files do not record an exact ExLlamaV3
revision. They are not unmodified ExLlamaV3 source files: Maya supplies its own
kernel organization, split scheduling, activation handling and workspaces;
Fastllm adds the integration and local changes listed below.

Provenance: ExLlamaV3 -> Project Maya/Strata -> Fastllm.
The direct import remains pinned to the Maya revision below; its original
hashes and both projects' copyright and permission notices are retained.

Imported from Project Maya v1.1.44, commit
5d20b0e8fd7c15fde2a9f2b4eac5e9776883690b
https://github.com/mw00/project-maya/tree/5d20b0e8fd7c15fde2a9f2b4eac5e9776883690b

Source paths: src/kernels/cuda/exl3.cu, src/kernels/cuda/exl3_legacy.cu,
include/strata/kernels/exl3.hpp and include/strata/kernels/dp4a.hpp.
Original file hashes are recorded in UPSTREAM.json.

Project Maya/Strata: MIT, copyright (c) 2026 Peasant Smith and the Project Maya
contributors; copyright (c) 2026 Niko1221 and Strata contributors.
The complete upstream license is LICENSE.
The upstream comments credit the EXL3 format, tensor-core tile decoding and
fused MoE design to ExLlamaV3 (Turboderp). Its MIT license is preserved as
LICENSE.exllamav3. See https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3 .

Local changes for Fastllm:
- optional indirect gate/up/down pointers for existing independent allocations;
- optional BF16 rounding at Fastllm MoE tensor boundaries;
- distinct workspaces for host threads using CUDA per-thread default streams;
- optional native F16/BF16 activation loads and output stores in modern and legacy
  decode kernels, preserving F32 accumulation and the existing rounding boundary;
- exl3_io.cuh is a Fastllm-authored storage-conversion helper, not an upstream file.
  This removes separate adapter cast kernels and their temporary buffers.
All options default to the upstream semantics. The Fastllm adapter lives in
src/devices/cuda/linear/fastllm-linear-exl3-maya.cu. CPU operators and fallback
CUDA operators are Fastllm's independent implementation, not imported Maya code.

2026-11-07 Fastllm hybrid-cache extension (local changes, not upstream Maya):
- Optional MoeArgs::route_output preserves the existing decode/rotation and
  BF16 boundaries while returning one weighted FP32 output per route.
- This mode omits the upstream cross-expert counter/reduction and disables
  split-input down projection. Fastllm combines resident, streamed and CPU
  experts in its own deterministic reducer. Existing callers default off.
- Optional scratch_lane separates shared, resident and staged graph branches
  on one captured stream. Default lane 0 retains the upstream workspace key.
2026-11-07 grouped output-projection adapter:
- Fastllm submits the independent EXL3 WoA slices through the existing upstream
  multi-job mv API, with separate input/output offsets and row strides.
- This adapter change does not modify the upstream matrix kernels or their
  split policy. Portable CUDA and CPU grouped fallbacks are Fastllm code.

2026-11-07 single-token BF16 specialization (Fastllm local changes):
- Enable the existing single-row scratch/accumulator specialization for CUDA.
- Specialize mul1 jobs with BF16 input and output at compile time, removing
  unused F32/F16/q8 input paths from those kernels. Other jobs keep the generic
  I/O path; multi-row jobs and the input-split planner are unchanged.
- Preserve FP32 accumulation, split reduction order, BF16 output rounding,
  all supported CUDA architectures.
No new upstream code is imported by this optimization. The import revision,
upstream hashes and both MIT license files above remain unchanged.

2026-11-07 cleanup (Fastllm local changes):
- Select single-row specialization and legacy/modern CUDA decode automatically.
- Keep the legacy gate/up scratch-capacity fallback without an A/B environment
  switch. Existing architecture and numerical fallback kernels remain available.
- Name ExLlamaV3 as the primary algorithm reference while retaining the Maya
  import provenance, local modifications and both MIT license files.
